newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees Asia-Pacific orders up 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees Asia-Pacific orders up 30 pct.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG said it expected its incoming orders from the Asia-Pacific region to rise 30 percent in 1995/96 to 15 billion marks.
The company said it plans to invest two billion to three billion dollars in the Asia-Pacific region by the year 2000.
Guenter Wilhelm, executive committee member responsible for the Asia-Pacific, also said the company was aiming for business volume of $17 billion in the region by 2000.
Wilhelm made his remarks at a news conference in Penang, Malaysia. A summary was distributed by the company.
"Siemens is growing faster in Asia-Pacific than anywhere else in the world," the statement quoted Wilhelm as saying.

"Within the next ten years, Asia-Pacific will comprise nearly half of the world electrical market with annual growth rates of some 10 percent. Our goal is to continue growing faster than our respective markets," he said.
Siemens is making opto-electronics in Penang, coal-fired power plants for China and telecommunications systems throughout the hemisphere.
Its investments in the region to date total $1.5 billion. Its Asia-Pacific workforce of 45,000 is projected to rise to 70,000 by 2000.
Siemens' business year ends on September 30.
